text: E. J. Lowe's ___ ontology recognizes four irreducible categories, substances, kinds, attributes, and modes, arranged in what he calls the ontological square.
explanation: Lowe's neo-Aristotelian system treats substances, kinds, attributes, and modes as mutually irreducible, with substances instantiating kinds, attributes characterizing kinds, and modes instantiating attributes. It contrasts with one- or two-category ontologies (such as pure bundle theory) that try to reduce this structure.
